Bitcoin just slid to about $55,000 — its lowest since September 2024 — and anyone holding a crypto ETF inside a brokerage or retirement account felt it too.

BTC fell as low as $55,106 early Saturday before clawing back near $60,000. It now trades roughly 52% below its $126,080 record set Oct. 6, 2025 (24/7 Wall St., Nov. 21).

More than $2.4 billion in leveraged crypto bets were wiped out in 24 hours (CoinGlass, via CoinDesk) — one of the biggest liquidation days on record, as forced selling fed on itself. US spot-bitcoin ETFs saw hundreds of millions in outflows this week, and those funds now sit in ordinary accounts on both sides of the border.

My take: leverage is what turns a dip into a cascade — the people hurt worst this weekend are the ones who borrowed to bet, not the ones who simply held.

Do you hold any crypto, directly or through an ETF — and did this weekend change your plans?
